summary.one_liner: GPT Pilot is a Python CLI research project from Pythagora that uses LLM agents to build apps step by step with a developer overseeing, and its repo is no longer maintained and had malicious code removed.
summary.what_it_does: GPT Pilot runs a pipeline of LLM agents (product owner, specification writer, architect, tech lead, developer, code monkey, reviewer, troubleshooter, debugger, technical writer) that turn an app name and description into generated code, one development task at a time. It supports OpenAI, Anthropic and Groq as LLM providers, with Azure and OpenRouter reachable through the openai setting. Configuration lives in config.json, with SQLite by default and optional PostgreSQL. Projects can be listed, resumed from the latest or a specific step, and deleted via CLI flags. Generated code is written into a workspace folder, and the README says the tool filters code so each LLM call only sees relevant files. The README also describes it as the core of the Pythagora VS Code extension. The README states the repository is no longer maintained. It also reports that malicious code (a credential-stealing worm hidden in core/telemetry/) was present from August 2025 to 11 June 2026 and was removed; anyone who ran the source in that window should rotate credentials and check listed indicators of compromise.
use_cases: generate a full app from a text description with an LLM
resume or roll back an AI-generated project step by step
use an LLM coding assistant from the command line
experiment with multi-agent code generation workflows
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into gpt-pilot
python3 -m venv venv and activate it
cp example-config.json config.json and set LLM provider key and database settings
python main.py to start GPT Pilot
python main.py --list, --project <app_id>, or --delete <app_id> to manage projects
notable: Builds apps incrementally with agent roles (developer, reviewer, debugger) rather than generating a whole codebase at once
Can resume a project from a specific earlier step, which deletes later progress
Backs the Pythagora VS Code extension
Filters code so each LLM request includes only the files relevant to the current task
caveats: Repository is no longer actively maintained
Malicious commit (credential stealer in core/telemetry/) was present from August 2025 to 11 June 2026; anyone who ran the code in that window should rotate credentials and check for compromise
Requires an LLM API key and Python 3.9+ setup
